{{Quote|Ulic Qel-Droma, Jedi and traitor&hellip;you will stand trial&hellip;and you will be ''sentenced to death''.|Sidrona|<ref name="TSW2" />}}
The '''Trial of Ulic Qel-Droma''' was a criminal proceeding carried out in [[3996 BBY]], which followed the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma's]] arrest and subsequent charge of perpetrating a menace to [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Galactic community|society]]. He was taken into custody by the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Knights]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] after being abandoned by an accomplice, the [[Sith sorcerer|Sith sorceress]] [[Aleema Keto]], following their [[Krath/Legends|Krath]] [[Sith cult/Legends|cult's]] [[Battle of Coruscant (Great Sith War)|failed surprise attack]] on the galactic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Qel-Droma was immediately placed under the jurisdiction of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] Sidrona, who chided that [[Death/Legends|death]] was the planned and acceptable restitution for the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] Lord's crimes against the citizens of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]].

Qel-Droma was shortly thereafter brought into the [[Grand Convocation Chamber|center]] of the [[Senate Hall]] to stand before the Republic's Senate, where a list of offenses was read by Sidrona for all to hear. When asked to enter a plea on his own behalf, Qel-Droma denounced those present as short-sighted individuals who only served as obstacles in the way of the [[Brotherhood of the Sith|Sith Brotherhood's]] plan to restore a [[Golden Age of the Sith|Golden Age]] of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] splendor through conquest of the galaxy. It was then that Qel-Droma's [[Sith Master/Legends|Master]], [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]], arrived with [[Mandalore the Indomitable]] and a cadre of [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] warriors at his side to take control of the judicial proceedings.

A [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith spell]] invoked by Exar Kun prevented anyone from intervening as the Dark Lord [[Telekinesis/Legends|freed]] Qel-Droma and made his way to the Chancellor's podium. The present [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] Knights were detained by the Massassi while Kun accosted Sidrona and, through the influence of his sorcery, [[Qâzoi Kyantuska|forced]] him to profess both the insignificance of the Republic and the superiority of the Brotherhood of the Sith. Kun then murdered the Chancellor before the impotent masses, effectively eliminating the judge and jury whose determination it was to see Ulic Qel-Droma found guilty for his infractions. With none left to oppose them, the accused and his comrades prepared to depart but were delayed by the sudden arrival of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Vodo-Siosk Baas]]. The [[Krevaaki]] Master attempted to reason with the Sith, but he too met his demise on the floor of the Senate Chamber in a [[Duel in the Senate|duel]] with Exar Kun. The events that unfolded during Ulic Qel-Droma's trial only served as proof of what both he and Kun had previously stated: that the Galactic Republic was powerless against the machinations of the Sith.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|Now I remember&mdash;he is a Jedi! Our enemy is Ulic Qel-Droma! We must report this to Coruscant at once. This is a dark day for the Republic.|[[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Orley Vanicus]]|<ref name="TSW1">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 1]]</ref>}}
[[File:QelDromaVsJedi-TSW2.jpg|thumb|left|270px|Ulic Qel-Droma is arrested by the Jedi Knights.]]
In [[3996 BBY]], the warrior clans of [[Mandalore the Indomitable]] led an unprovoked attack on the seven [[Planet/Legends|planets]] of the [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Empress Teta star system]]. This onslaught brought the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] into direct conflict with the system's governing body, the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]-inspired [[Krath/Legends|Krath]] [[Sith cult/Legends|cult]]. In response, [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] and Krath leader [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]] accepted a challenge of personal combat against Mandalore with control of either man's factions wagered as spoils for the victor. Qel-Droma triumphed over his opponent [[Battle of Kuar|in battle]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kuar]]'s [[plains of Harkul]], and he absorbed both Mandalore and his [[Army/Legends|armies]] into the ranks of the Krath. Under Qel-Droma's heel, the combined Mandalorian and Tetan forces then commenced a series of raids on several instrumental [[Starship/Legends|starship]] construction facilities under the service of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] which were designed to augment the strength of the Sith military forces in preparation for an all-out war against their enemies. Plunder, destruction, and the [[Death/Legends|deaths]] of innocents were their trademarks, and the swift efficiency with which Qel-Droma's force operated left the Republic unable to determine the identities of the aggressors at each turn. It was not until the Krath legions carried out an [[Battle of Foerost (Great Sith War)|assault]] on the [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]] at [[Foerost/Legends|Foerost]] did the Republic learn that, much to their dismay, [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] expatriate Ulic Qel-Droma had been the mastermind behind these acts of [[Pirate/Legends|piracy]].<ref name="TSW1" />

Following the terrorist attacks on the Republic shipyards, Qel-Droma's next offense, a [[Battle of Coruscant (Great Sith War)|surprise attack]] on the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], ended in folly. He was betrayed and intentionally abandoned to his own resources by his lover, the [[Sith sorcerer|Krath witch]] [[Aleema Keto]], even as victory was in his grasp. Before he could escape, he was arrested by [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Knights]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] to which he had once belonged. They [[Prison/Legends|imprisoned]] him within a [[wall of light]]&mdash;a fortress of [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light-side]] [[The Force/Legends|Force energy]] that blocked access to his [[Force power/Legends|Jedi powers]]. Custody of Qel-Droma was then given over to [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Sidrona]], who declared that not only would the Sith Lord stand trial for his crimes against the galaxy, he would most assuredly be executed for them as well.<ref name="TSW2" />

==The trial==
===The trial begins===
{{Quote|Ulic Qel-Droma, you are a threat to the peace and security of the Galactic Republic. Your list of crimes is long&mdash;the destruction of shipyards, the looting of supply bases, the enslavement of mercenaries. And, even worse&mdash;you have betrayed your training as a Jedi Knight&mdash;your vow to protect the Republic! How do you plead?''"<br />"''I don't plead with fools. You are puppets of tradition pretending to be important. The coming Golden Age has no place for you. Your Republic is an empty, self-indulgent diversion&hellip;signifying ''nothing''.|Sidrona and Ulic Qel-Droma|<ref name="TSW3" />}}
[[File:WaitingForSentencing.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Ulic Qel-Droma awaits his trial]]
Ulic Qel-Droma was shackled and confined in total darkness within a cell until the hour of his arraignment. He was then escorted by a pair of [[Republic soldier]]s into the [[Grand Convocation Chamber]] of the [[Senate Hall]] and led to the center of the auditorium to face the entirety of the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] that would oversee the criminal procedure. The Supreme Chancellor of the Republic, who presided over the trial as both judge and jury, towered over Qel-Droma on a podium much larger than the one on which the accused stood.<ref name="TSW3" />

Prosecution began without any further delay as Qel-Droma stood silently listening to Sidrona recite a long list of offenses. Destruction of Republic property, terrorism, and [[Slavery/Legends|enslavement]] were among them; the most damning, however, was the accusation that Ulic Qel-Droma had forsaken his commitment of sworn service to the Galactic Republic as a Knight of the Jedi Order. When asked to enter a plea on his own behalf, the Sith Lord remained defiant and refused to even acknowledge the authority of the court. He instead excoriated the entire Republic as a self-serving, meaningless organization, one that was insignificant in the [[Golden Age of the Sith|Golden Age]] that was to be restored by the efforts of the [[Brotherhood of the Sith]]. His claim rocked the Senate Chamber and horrified all those present, including Jedi Knights [[Nomi Sunrider]] and [[Sylvar]], whose heads hung in shame at their [[Dark Jedi/Legends|fallen]] comrade's proclamation. His own brother, [[Cay Qel-Droma|Cay]], was also in attendance and rushed the Senate floor in disbelief of what he believed to be Ulic's Sith delusions. Cay attempted to enter a plea of trial incompetence for his brother but was rebuked by the same man on whose behalf he was trying to intercede.<ref name="TSW3" />

===Sith objections===
{{Main|Duel in the Senate}}
{{Quote|Excuse me, might I join the discussion? I've got something I'm sure you'll find interesting.|Exar Kun|<ref name="TSW3" />}}
[[File:CourtRoomMockery.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Exar Kun makes a mockery of Ulic Qel-Droma's trial.]]
Having discovered the nature of Aleema's betrayal, Mandalore the Indomitable prepared to rescue Qel-Droma by first going to [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] and requesting assistance from Qel-Droma's superior, [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]]. The pair then traveled with Kun's [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] warriors to Coruscant and stormed the Senate Hall in the midst of Qel-Droma's trial. Immediately seizing control of the trial's attendees, Kun petrified the entire Senate body through a [[Qâzoi Kyantuska|mind control spell]] and simultaneously [[Telekinesis/Legends|used the Force to remove]] Qel-Droma's restraints. The enthralled [[Senator/Legends|senators]] of the Republic could do nothing to prevent Kun's interruption, but the unaffected Jedi rushed the Senate floor in opposition of the intruders. Nomi Sunrider pleaded for the defendant to entertain reason while Sylvar slaughtered several Massassi in combat. Kun, meanwhile, ascended the podium of the Chancellor, who himself called for his guards. When Sidrona realized their failure to respond, he futilely attempted to defend himself against Exar Kun, but the Dark Lord blocked the attack and bored his fingers into Sidrona's skull, forcing him to repeat the words of Kun's plan for galactic conquest to a captive audience as though he were a puppet. Kun closed by stating that his actions thus far had been a demonstration of the Republic's uselessness and that the Republic did not even factor into the Brotherhood's grand design of a galaxy ruled under the magnificence of a Sith Golden Age. He released his Force-empowered grip on Sidrona, whose lifeless body fell to the floor in a pool of his own [[Blood/Legends|blood]]. Kun then prepared to depart with his associates. When it appeared that no one dared to stand in the way, however, [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Vodo-Siosk Baas]] arrived and barred their exit. Not to be hindered, Exar Kun exchanged several words with his former teacher before the two of them engaged in a [[Duel in the Senate|vicious duel]]. Kun was ultimately victorious, slaying the [[Krevaaki]] Master on the floor of the Senate Chamber. With the trial effectively over, Ulic Qel-Droma was absolved of guilt by his [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]]. Together, they left to continue the [[Great Sith War/Legends|war]] that they believed would precede the Sith dynasty wherein they intended to rule the galaxy.<ref name="TSW3" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|I've searched the galaxy for some way that I might become a Jedi again&hellip;that I might somehow be forgiven and earn back my powers. But I am blind and deaf to the Force&hellip;I can sense nothing here&hellip;other than the sadness and destruction that my own eyes tell me.|Ulic Qel-Droma|<ref name="TSW6">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 6|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 6]]</ref>}}
[[File:SadUlicIsSad-TOTJTSW6.jpg|thumb|right|170px|Ulic Qel-Droma, broken and remorseful for his life as a Sith Lord]]
Following the Sith Brotherhood's flight from Coruscant and return to [[Temple of Exar Kun|Exar Kun's temple]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], Mandalore the Indomitable made Ulic Qel-Droma aware of Aleema Keto's attempt to leave him stranded on Coruscant. Qel-Droma realized that the Tetan [[Emperor/Legends|empress]] had manipulated their partnership since its inception, and her actions on Coruscant were a result of her desire to eliminate the Sith Lord so that she might assume sole leadership of the Krath. He dealt with Aleema's treachery by allowing her to lead [[Battle of Kemplex Nine|the next offensive]] on the [[Kemplex Nine]] [[Space station/Legends|jump station]], where she used an ancient Sith [[Superweapon/Legends|weapon]] far beyond her capabilities of controlling. The [[Cron Supernova/Legends|supernova]] that she [[Supernova (Sith magic)|caused]] annihilated her enemies, but consumed her as well&mdash;just as Qel-Droma had planned.<ref name="TSW4">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 4]]</ref>

Exar Kun continued to lead the Great Sith War with Ulic Qel-Droma at his side, defeating the Republic and Jedi repeatedly in battle, and they believed the Sith Brotherhood would indeed conquer the galaxy just as Kun had declared at Qel-Droma's trial. When the [[Supernova/Legends|supernova]] that resulted from Aleema Keto's misuse of Sith powers at Kemplex Nine forced the Jedi to evacuate the library world of [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]], Kun and Qel-Droma led their forces in an [[Battle of Ossus (Great Sith War)|invasion]] of the planet. While Exar Kun counted on the conflagration providing him with an opportunity to pilfer as much [[Jedi artifact/Legends|Jedi lore]] as he could obtain, he had not expected that Qel-Droma would ultimately betray him. After murdering his brother Cay in a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]] and being totally [[Sever Force/Legends|stripped]] of the Force by an outraged Nomi Sunrider,<ref name="TSW5">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 5|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 5]]</ref> Ulic renounced his [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] ways and turned on Kun by assisting the Jedi in his [[Battle of Yavin 4 (Great Sith War)|final defeat]] at Yavin 4. Because of this, the vision of a Sith Golden Age spoken of by the Dark Lord during Qel-Droma's trial never came to pass.<ref name="TSW6" />

The ease with which Exar Kun entered the Convocation Chamber of the Senate to disrupt the trial of Ulic Qel-Droma caused the Galactic Republic to take preventative measures against such travesties from ever happening again. A modernized facility was constructed to replace the Senate Hall as the new venue for governmental affairs, but the Hall itself remained as a place of ceremonial reverence, occasionally used to house important high-profile events due to its large seating capacity. [[3963 BBY|Thirty-three]] years after Ulic Qel-Droma's trial, the Senate [[Trial of Demagol|convened again]] to determine the fate of another galactic criminal: the Mandalorian [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Demagol]].<ref name="Kotor47">[[Knights of the Old Republic 47|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 47]]</ref>

==Principal participants==
===Galactic Republic===
====Sidrona====
{{Main|Sidrona}}
{{Quote|I just wanted to say that you, and the whole Republic Senate, are ''irrelevant''. The Jedi Knights have coddled you for centuries.|Exar Kun, to Sidrona|<ref name="TSW3" />}}
[[File:VodoAndSidrona.jpg|220px|left]]
Sidrona was the Supreme Chancellor of the Republic during the Sith War. He was present on Coruscant when his friend Vodo-Siosk Baas arrived to discuss the possibility of Jedi involvement in the terrorist attacks that had been plaguing the Republic, though he was reluctant to believe what he perceived as a rumor. The Chancellor's worst fears were realized, however, when [[Minister of Defense (Republic)|Minister of Defense]] [[Netus]] confirmed the criminal's identity as that of Ulic Qel-Droma. After the battle of Coruscant and Qel-Droma's subsequent apprehension, Sidrona felt that a preponderance of the overwhelming evidence would be enough to sway the Senators into accepting a proposition of capital punishment as penance for Ulic Qel-Droma's crimes.<ref name="TSW2" />

====Cay Qel-Droma====
{{Main|Cay Qel-Droma}}
{{Quote|Just trying to help my own brother.|Cay Qel-Droma|<ref name="TSW3" />}}
[[File:CayAtUlicsTrial-TheSithWar3.jpg|140px|left]]
The younger son of Jedi Master [[Lien-Tsai Qel-Droma]],<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref> Cay was one of the Jedi who, alongside his brother, were regarded as heroes following their success in eradicating the [[Japrael system/Legends|Onderon system]] of the oppression of the Sith.<ref name="BWOO">''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Ulic Qel-Droma and the Beast Wars of Onderon]]''</ref><ref name="FNU">''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising]]''</ref> Cay was hesitant to allow his brother to embark on a lone [[Mission to Empress Teta|infiltration mission]] to the Empress Teta system,<ref name="DLOTS4">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 4|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 4]]</ref> and was devastated to learn that the mission resulted in his older brother's fall to the dark side of the Force.<ref name="DLOTS5">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 5|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 5]]</ref> He also found it difficult to fathom Ulic as capable of committing the atrocities that he was accused of against the very Republic he had sworn to protect as a Jedi Knight.<ref name="TSW2" /> At Ulic's trial, Cay was dumbfounded when he heard his brother's response to the charges levied against him. He implored the senators to ignore Ulic's delusional tirade, but to no avail; Exar Kun had already arrived and incapacitated all the attendees of the trial with his Sith sorcery. Cay was among those who watched helplessly as Kun freed his brother and killed both Sidrona and Jedi Master Baas.<ref name="TSW3" />

===Brotherhood of the Sith===
====Exar Kun====
{{Main|Exar Kun/Legends}}
{{Quote|We did all this to show you how useless and ineffective the Republic is. We don't ''want'' your cooperation. The Republic is not even part of the plan.|Exar Kun, after the murder of Sidrona|<ref name="TSW3" />}}
[[File:MandyTheExtremelyDomitableAndExarKun-TSW3.jpg|190px|left]]
Exar Kun was once a Jedi apprentice under Master Vodo-Siosk Baas on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]]<ref name="DLOTS1">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 1|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 1]]</ref> whose curiosity about the ways of renegade Jedi led him into a quest to acquire Sith knowledge on his own, against the suggestions of his former teacher.<ref name="DLOTSA">[[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith'' audio drama]]</ref> Kun found that which he sought and embraced the dark side,<ref name="DLOTS3">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 3|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 3]]</ref> eventually becoming Lord of the Sith.<ref name="DLOTS6">[[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 6|''Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith'' 6]]</ref> As the new Dark Lord, Exar Kun embarked on a campaign with Ulic Qel-Droma's Krath to destroy the Republic in preparation for the re-institution of a Sith Golden Age. Patience and meticulous calculation were his tools though, and he spoke against the hasty invasion of Coruscant<ref name="TSW1" /> that ultimately resulted in Qel-Droma's arrest.<ref name="TSW2" /> Nevertheless, when Mandalore the Indomitable arrived on Yavin 4 requesting Kun's assistance in liberating Qel-Droma from the clutches of the Republic, the Dark Lord obliged. He believed that the Republic was powerless against what was to come and demonstrated their impotence upon his arrival in the Senate Hall when he freed Qel-Droma, murdered the Supreme Chancellor, and killed Vodo-Siosk Baas shortly thereafter.<ref name="TSW3" />

====Ulic Qel-Droma====
{{Main|Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends}}
{{Quote|If you expect me to repent, you'll be sorely disappointed. Stopping us now will be like standing at the bottom of a mountain trying to stop an ''avalanche''.|Ulic Qel-Droma|<ref name="TSW3" />}}
[[File:UlicQelDroma-TOTJTSW5.jpg|180px|left]]
Former Jedi Knight Ulic Qel-Droma was once a hero of the Galactic Republic;<ref name="FNU" /> however, his transgressions as a Dark Lord of the Sith far overshadowed any benevolence that had previously been associated with his character.<ref name="TSW1" /> Regardless of the headstrong assessment given by both his former Jedi allies<ref name="TOTJA">[[Tales of the Jedi (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi'' audio drama]]</ref> and his current Sith Master Exar Kun,<ref name="TSW3" /> Qel-Droma believed that he and his Krath forces were powerful enough to overthrow the seat of the Galactic Republic on Coruscant itself. He had not counted on the treachery of Aleema Keto, which led to his arrest<ref name="TSW2" /> and subsequent trial as a war criminal.<ref name="TSW3" /> Even after being temporarily blocked from his Force powers<ref name="TSW2" /> and forced to answer to the Republic Senate for his actions, Qel-Droma remained indignant and determined to show the Republic that their demise was at hand. To see their former comrade and loved one behave in this manner was enough to deeply upset the Jedi, although their expressed distress did little to sway him from the destiny he had chosen for himself.<ref name="TSW3" />

==Behind the scenes==
Veteran [[Star Wars]] author [[Kevin J. Anderson]] penned the issue in which the trial of Ulic Qel-Droma appeared, being the [[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 3|third]] in ''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|Tales of the Jedi's]] [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War|Sith War]]'' story arc, titled the same as the actual event. Aleema Keto's betrayal of Ulic in the [[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 2|previous issue]] served as the plot device which allowed for Ulic's capture and prosecution in ''The Trial of Ulic Qel-Droma'' issue. Qel-Droma would return the favor in the next installment, [[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 4|''Jedi Holocaust'']]. Aside from its comic appearances, the trial was also mentioned in several pieces of source material, including both the [[The Dark Side Sourcebook|''Dark Side'']] and ''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]s'' and the [[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''Essential'']] and [[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''New Essential Chronologies'']] as well.

The [[Star Wars Insider 26|''Star Wars Insider'' 26]] article [[The Horse's Mouth|''Straight from the Horse's Mouth: A Guide to the Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi Universe, Part 1'']] says that the trial took place in [[3991 BBY]],<ref name="insider">{{InsiderCite|26|The Horse's Mouth|Straight from the Horse's Mouth: A Guide to the ''Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi'' Universe, Part 1}}</ref> while ''The New Essential Chronology'' places the event at 3996 BBY.<ref name="NEC" /> As ''Insider 26'' contradicts many other established dates,<ref name="insider" /> this article treats ''The New Essential Chronology''  as being correct.
